name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3487
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: A bit of zesty sex with, um, a deer maybe? That's almost certain to end badly for someone

definitions.text: That's almost certain to end badly for someone

indicators.note: a small bit of a word is taken here as just its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of zesty
Eros is the god of desire, standing for sex
taken as written
deer are hunted as game, so a deer is an example of game

explanation.surface: A racy, absurd tale of an encounter with a deer, followed by a warning that this can only end in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the pieces. In a zero-sum game every gain is matched by someone else's loss, so the definition is a playful description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: In a zero-sum contest the winnings of one side equal the losses of the other, so some participant is bound to lose out.

clue.text: "Heavy Metal": possible name for Zorro's company?

blocks.note: Zorro famously slashes a Z as his mark
Inc. is the abbreviation for incorporated, a company

explanation.surface: Suggesting a band name, Heavy Metal, for a firm owned by the masked swordsman Zorro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy Metal' looks like the music genre, but it is a kind of chemical element; Zorro's firm would be Z Inc.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a dense metallic element often grouped among the heavy metals in environmental science.

clue.text: Criticizes Confederate instruments

blocks.note: Reb, short for rebel, was a Confederate soldier
ukes is short for ukuleles

explanation.surface: Someone finding fault with instruments from the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke is to reprimand or scold sharply, so rebukes matches criticizes as a verb.

clue.text: Large reptile, turning up like this, becomes gold and red

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up makes the letters climb from bottom to top, so they read backwards

blocks.note: so means in this manner
gets as in 'gets cold', meaning becomes
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
R is the abbreviation for red

explanation.surface: A big lizard rolling over and changing colour to gold and red.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'like this, becomes' is turned round; gold and red follow in order. 'And' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stegosaur is a plated dinosaur, a huge extinct reptile of the Jurassic period.

clue.text: In France, one breaks most wild horses

indicators.note: one thing breaking into another sits inside it
wild suggests disorder, so the word it describes is rearranged

blocks.note: un is French for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French horseman breaking in the wildest of the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' fits horse taming, but it means one piece breaks into the jumbled other.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounts are animals that are ridden, so the word serves as a general term for riding horses.

clue.text: Pastoral rainbow over a goddess, for the most part

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first
only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a rainbow forms an arc
taken as written
Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt

explanation.surface: A country scene with a rainbow arching above a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadian describes an idealised rustic life, after Arcadia, the Greek region of shepherds.

clue.text: Pennsylvania city is home to no puppet

indicators.note: a place that is home to something holds it within

blocks.note: Erie is a city in northwest Pennsylvania
N is the abbreviation for no, as on a yes/no form

explanation.surface: A claim that a Pennsylvania city has no puppets at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' reads as a negative but is just its abbreviation. Ernie is Bert's roommate on Sesame Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is the Muppet character from Sesame Street, a famous hand puppet.

clue.text: Invert the second number and letter — that is one way to look smart

indicators.note: to invert something is to turn it upside down, so these letters are read in the opposite order

blocks.note: the second counting number
'second' serves twice: the second letter of the alphabet
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: An instruction for some puzzle trick with numbers and letters, and then a remark on looking sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'second' is shared: it picks out both the number two and the letter B. Only those two pieces are turned round; 'that is' then follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow tie is a piece of neckwear worn with formal or dressy clothes, so wearing one is a way of appearing smart.

clue.text: Social gathering to raise Norwegian male cattle

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters lifts them from bottom to top, so they read backwards

blocks.note: a bee is a gathering for work or fun, as in a quilting bee
Olaf is a typical Norwegian man's name

explanation.surface: A party thrown to breed bulls in Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' looks like stock breeding but turns the Norwegian name upside down; 'to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefalo are a breed of livestock produced by crossing bison with domestic cows.

clue.text: Triumph over exotic termite when it is cold

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first
exotic means strange or foreign, so the word's letters are made unfamiliar

blocks.note: to triumph is to win
taken as written

explanation.surface: Beating a foreign termite infestation once the weather turns chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintertime is the season of winter, the period of the year when the weather is coldest.

clue.text: High-born snob lectures participant

indicators.note: a participant takes part, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An aristocratic snob lecturing the other people at an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Participant' looks like a person in the scene, but it says the answer is a part within 'snob lectures'.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes someone of aristocratic birth or rank, which is what high-born means.

clue.text: Vessel protecting North Carolina, formerly, with lack of interest

indicators.note: something protecting other things wraps around them, so the vessel goes on the outside

blocks.note: an urn is a vase or container
the postal abbreviation for North Carolina
once means at some earlier time

explanation.surface: A ship guarding the North Carolina coast in days past, while nobody much cared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship but is a pot, an urn, which wraps around the state abbreviation and 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is indifference, a noun for the state of not caring or being uninterested.

clue.text: Snarled: "Another Kennedy coming after $1,000"

indicators.note: one piece coming after another is simply placed behind it in the sequence

blocks.note: K stands for a thousand, as in a salary of 50K
a different Kennedy is one who is not Ted, the senator

explanation.surface: Someone growling that yet another Kennedy has turned up with a big donation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarled' looks like an angry speech tag, but it means tangled. Ted Kennedy was a long-serving US senator; any other Kennedy is 'not Ted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarled can describe hair or rope that is tangled, the same as knotted.

clue.text: Fill with happiness and marvel at exquisite cargo

indicators.note: cargo is what a vehicle carries inside it, so the answer is carried within these words

blocks.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled and admiring a ship's beautiful freight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cargo' seems to be what is marvelled at, but it is the signal that the answer sits inside the preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to make someone joyful or in high spirits, a verb for filling them with happiness.

clue.text: Get lost, assuming I am heading from Toronto to Rochester with a pet

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the outer word takes the rest inside it

blocks.note: scat is a command meaning go away
taken as written
Rochester, New York, lies east-southeast of Toronto across Lake Ontario

explanation.surface: Someone told to clear off, planning a trip across the lake with their animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get lost' looks like the definition, but it is the outer piece; the compass bearing between the two lakeside cities supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a popular domestic breed of cat, kept as a household companion animal.

clue.text: Tailor names one measurement

indicators.note: to tailor is to cut and alter, so the letters get refitted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tailor writing down a customer's name along with a single measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' fits the scene as a noun, but it is the verb signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The inseam is the length of a trouser leg's inner seam, a standard figure a tailor records.

clue.text: Tense about pros messing up travel document

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes around the second
messing up puts things into disorder, so those letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the past is a grammatical tense
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone anxious that professionals will make a mess of their travel papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous, but it is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official identity document needed to cross international borders.

clue.text: Don't start requesting something to keep you afloat for a surgical procedure

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: asking means requesting
a raft is a floating platform

explanation.surface: Advice not to begin asking for a life raft before an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin graft is an operation transplanting healthy skin to cover a wound or burn.

clue.text: Liquid sort of contains oxygen and hydrogen? Indeed

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so these letters can take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A question whether a liquid of some kind contains oxygen and hydrogen, which water certainly does.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemistry suggests water, but 'Liquid' is the signal to rearrange; 'contains' just adds the two symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsooth is an archaic adverb meaning in truth or truly, used to affirm a statement.

clue.text: Satellite conveying a coach's cookie

indicators.note: something conveying a load carries it inside, so one piece holds the others

blocks.note: the moon is Earth's natural satellite
taken as written
a railway coach is a car

explanation.surface: A spacecraft ferrying a sports coach's biscuit into orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a trainer, but here it is a railway car.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small sweet biscuit made with almonds or coconut, a type of cookie in American usage.

clue.text: Whim: Practice recklessly after time runs out

indicators.note: acting recklessly means acting without order, so the letters are scrambled
something that runs out leaves, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Acting on impulse: practising carelessly once the clock has run down.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a sudden, unpredictable change of mind or behaviour, the same impulse as a whim.

clue.text: Someone harmed Victor and Timothy

indicators.note: and adds one item to another, placing them side by side

blocks.note: Vic is a short form of Victor
Tim is a short form of Timothy

explanation.surface: A report that two named men, Victor and Timothy, were hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is a person who has been injured or wronged by another or by events.

clue.text: Barb, claiming connection, is a second-rater

indicators.note: claiming something means taking it in and holding it

blocks.note: a thorn is a sharp barb on a plant
an in is a useful connection, as in 'she has an in at the studio'

explanation.surface: Someone named Barb who boasts of insider contacts is dismissed as mediocre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barb' looks like a woman's name, but it is a spike.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinhorn is an American slang term for a pretentious but cheap and inferior person.

clue.text: Hits comparatively ancient receptacle

blocks.note: H is the baseball box-score abbreviation for hits
older is the comparative of old

explanation.surface: A batter striking an antique pot.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hits comes from baseball scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder is anything designed to hold something else, such as a container or stand.

clue.text: Excellent purse is ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so its letters fall into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sarcastic 'great!' on discovering one's handbag is spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds ironic; the first word is a plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal adjective of praise meaning very good or first-rate.

clue.text: Awesome sequel for Bones?

blocks.note: rad is slang for excellent or awesome
a sequel is often numbered with the Roman numeral two

explanation.surface: Hoping for a cool follow-up series to the TV show Bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' looks like the title of the TV crime drama, but the definition is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii is the plural of radius, the forearm bone, so it names a set of bones.

clue.text: Small cut of meat infused with, for instance, liqueur

indicators.note: something infused with another has it steeped inside, so the second piece goes within the first

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
loin is a cut from the back of an animal
e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: A dainty piece of meat marinated in something like a liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for 'for instance' slips into the cut of meat after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloe gin is a red liqueur made by steeping sloe berries in gin with sugar.

clue.text: Wealthy people embracing publicity

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the answer is held inside the words before it

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: The rich happily welcoming media attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wealthy people' reads as the subject, but it is the place the answer hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is exaggerated promotion or media attention used to build public interest.

clue.text: Julia, a gangster in the early days

blocks.note: Julia Child was the famous American TV chef
a hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster

explanation.surface: Julia was a mobster back when she was young.
explanation.walkthrough: Julia Child, the American cookery writer and TV chef, supplies her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Childhood is the period of being a child, the earliest years of a person's life.

clue.text: Decapitate Venetian villain, leading to New York's suffering

indicators.note: cutting off the head means losing the first letter of the following name
leading to places the first piece in front of what comes next

blocks.note: Iago is the villain of Othello, set in Venice
the standard abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: Beheading a Venetian villain causes pain in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago is Shakespeare's schemer in Othello, the Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme physical or mental pain, a noun for great suffering.

clue.text: See 7
Entire chain is broken? That's what you get

indicators.note: something broken comes apart and is reassembled, so its letters move around

blocks.note: taken as written, both words used

explanation.surface: A complaint about a snapped chain, met with a shrug of 'that's what you get'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's what you get' sounds like a reproach, but it describes a bequest: what you receive when someone dies.
explanation.definitionFit: An inheritance is property or money received from a deceased relative, literally what an heir gets.
